key_insight: The paper shows that canonical lifted-product qLDPC codes can be co-designed with a structured logical basis that enables a full, low-overhead set of fault-tolerant logical operations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to modular quantum computation on ultra-high-rate codes, reducing the complexity of gates, measurements, and code-surgery workflows.
method: Define a canonical logical basis using cyclic symmetry in lifted-product codes
Build constant-depth logical Clifford gates via automorphisms and fold-transversal operations
Implement modular graph code surgery, parallel Pauli-product measurement, and magic-state injection using reusable seed gadgets or a compact extractor
evidence_signal: The abstract cites concrete large-code examples, including [[1122,148,≤20]] and [[4350,1224,≤20]] LP codes, with only 2 or 4 seed surgery gadgets and an extractor smaller than half the data block.
watch_item: The approach relies on specific cyclic-symmetry structure, so benefits may not directly transfer to arbitrary qLDPC codes without redesign.
paper_title: Logical computation with canonical lifted product codes
